text:
meera: quick terraform question — adding a KMS grant for an IRSA role, hitting weird deny in staging. snuck the change into infra-pr, can someone eyeball ordering/conds?

alex: can you paste the tf snippet you used? most ordering issues are just using role id vs arn or missing explicit depends_on.

meera: sure — gist of it: ```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "sa_role" {
  name = "svc-myapp-sa-role"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_assume.json
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "sa_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.app_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.sa_role.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey*"]
}
```

ryan: grantee_principal should be the role ARN, so that's fine. two gotchas: (1) the KMS key policy must allow the grant OR allow the role in principal list; (2) TF sometimes creates grant before role if references are subtle — add depends_on on the grant to the role to be explicit.

sam: also check the key's policy conditions — we had a key that checks StringEquals kms:CallerAccount or aws:PrincipalTag/session name and that caused denies when sessionname had slashes. any session name constraints?

meera: the deny in CloudTrail says "Access denied by key policy condition kms:RequestPrincipalSessionName" (paraphrased). I thought session name is just the pod SA name, but IRSA session names look like: "system:serviceaccount:ns:name:UUID" sometimes.

alex: yeah IRSA STS session name includes the sub claim by default which can include `system:serviceaccount/...` and that can have colons/slashes. If the key policy condition expects a short ascii token it can fail. Two options: relax the key policy to match the full principal ARN/role instead of session name, or use sts:TagSession to pass a sanitized tag and check that in policy.

ryan: example minimal fixes: change key policy to allow the role principal arn explicitly: ```json

{
  "Sid": "AllowRole",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {
    "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/svc-myapp-sa-role"
  },
  "Action": "kms:*",
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

ryan: and in TF, make the grant depend on the role creation: ```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "sa_decrypt" {
  # ...
  depends_on = [aws_iam_role.sa_role]
}
```

meera: ok that matches what I suspected. question: will granting to the role arn be stable if role is assumed by many pods with different session names?

alex: yes — KMS grants are tied to the principal (role) not the session name. the session name only matters if the key policy has extra conditions referencing it. Prefer allowing the role or using condition on aws:PrincipalArn rather than session name.

sam: FYI if you need to lock down further, we can tag the session and put a condition on aws:PrincipalTag/<tag> instead of using SessionName. but that requires the assume role to allow tagging: `sts:TagSession` in the trust policy and use `aws:PrincipalTag` in the key policy.

meera: nice — hadn't thought of TagSession. will try relaxing key policy to role arn first and add depends_on. pinging infra bot to run a quick plan validation.

infra-bot: plan started for branch infra/pr-422 — 5 resources to change, no cycles detected. (run id: infra-197246) :white_check_mark:

meera: thanks — i'll push the change with depends_on and policy tweak, and drop a follow-up if staging still chokes. :thumbsup:

alex: lmk if you want a hand with the tag flow, been down that path.

meera: will do, thanks everyone.
